MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 18, 2015

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Schlicht at 5:00 p.m., on May 18, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May 14, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager /Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Housing Authority: Conference with Real Property Negotiator Government Code
  Section 54956.8. The unimproved real property commonly referred to as “Site C”
  (City Housing Element) located on City-owned land directly adjacent to and
  southeasterly of the City’s Animal Service Center off Center Drive, and easterly of
  Saddleback College (Assessor Parcel No. 740-112-03). Mission Viejo Housing
  Authority Negotiators Dennis Wilberg, Executive Director, Keith Rattay, Cheryl

City Council Minutes  1  May 18, 2015
   Dyas, Elaine Lister, and Celeste Brady, Special Counsel. Negotiating Party: City of
  Mission Viejo.

CS2. City: Conference with Real Property Negotiator Government Code Section 54956.8.
  The unimproved real property commonly referred to as “Site C” (City Housing
  Element) located on City-owned land directly adjacent to and southeasterly of the
  City’s Animal Service Center off Center Drive, and easterly of Saddleback College
  (Assessor Parcel No. 740-112-03). Agency Negotiators Dennis Wilberg, City Manager,
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services, Cheryl Dyas,
  Director of Administrative Services, Elaine Lister, Director of Community
  Development, and William Curley, III, City Attorney. Negotiating Party: Mission
  Viejo Housing Authority under discussion price and terms.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Schlicht recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the two closed session items focused on real property
price and terms. The City Council reviewed the matter, asked questions and will address the topic
in a public session during item 24 this evening. At that time, the City Council will decide whether
or not to sell "Site C" to the Housing Authority.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Schlicht presented certificates of commendation to "Marine of the Quarter" Lance
  Corporal Cassadee B. Jackson and "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Sergeant
  Deonte L. Lang.

P2.  Recognize Mike Reiley and Outback Steakhouse for their Philanthropic Efforts for
  the City

  Mayor Schlicht presented the proclamation to Mike Reiley of Outback Steakhouse.

P3.  Recognize May 26 through September 1, 2015, for Drowning Prevention and
  Awareness

City Council Minutes  2  May 18, 2015
   Mayor Schlicht presented the proclamation to OCFA Chief Ken Harrison.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Chuck McCollough, Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce: outlined upcoming Chamber of
Commerce events including the monthly mixer hosted by the Nadadores on Thursday, May
21, and a ribbon cutting ceremony for Snow Station on June 5.

Dr. Casey Cooper, Ph.D., M.V.: shared her professional opinion on the Nadadores swim and dive
program from the perspective of a licensed sports psychologist. She stated that the Nadadores are
represented in every national and international competition and she encouraged the City Council
to vote yes on the renovations of the Nadadores facilities.

Jim Montrella, M.V.: referencing item 31, he asked that a 24-month window be given before the
program is implemented.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 4, 5, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, and 22 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate
discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the Consent
Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular meeting of May 4, 2015, as presented.

6.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Third Quarter of 2014-15

  Received and filed.

7.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March 2015
City Council Minutes  3  May 18, 2015
   Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March 2015

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March
  2015

  Received and filed.

10.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for March 2015

  Received and filed.

17.  Marguerite Parkway Median Island Via Florecer to Trabuco - (CIP 220) - Notice of
  Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful
  Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty- five (35) days respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City and (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of $32,677.37,
  thirty-five (35) days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

18.  Acceptance of Final Parcel Map 2013-120

  Approved Final Parcel Map 2013-120 and authorized the City Clerk and the City Engineer
  to sign the record map upon completion of any technical corrections required by the City
  Engineer.

19.  Requests by KSBR and Mission Viejo Rotary for a one-time exemption to the "No
  Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regula

  Approved requests by KSBR and Mission Viejo Rotary for a one-time exemption to the
  "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" regulation at City facilities.

20.  Annual Review of Residential and Commercial Integrated Waste Management Rates

  Adopted Resolution 15-21 Approving the Proposed Trash Rate Adjustments for
  Residential (.93% Increase From $12.79 to $12.91 per Month), Commercial (.98%
  Increase), and Roll-Off (1.09% Increase) Services Effective July 1, 2015.
City Council Minutes  4  May 18, 2015
 21.  2015 Fourth of July Community Street Faire

  Approved the Special Events Permit submitted by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee
  authorizing the annual Mission Viejo Fourth of July Community Street Faire on Saturday,
  July 4, 2015.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register Dated April 24, 2015 in the Amount of $2,929,090.03

  Mayor Schlicht inquired about several expenditures on the check register to which staff
  provided responses.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

4.  Check Register Dated May 1, 2015 in the Amount of $851,067.25

  Mayor Schlicht inquired about several expenditures on the check register and staff
  provided responses.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

5.  Quarterly Check Register Report - Third Quarter of FY 2014-15

  Mayor Schlicht asked why the CIP list was not included in the quarterly check register.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas responded that staff is still trying to build
  a report in the new financial software

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to receive and file.

City Council Minutes  5  May 18, 2015
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

11.  Unappropriation of Park Development Fees

  Council Member Sachs inquired about the number of bocce ball courts that are included in
  the budget.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that two courts
  are planned.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, adopt
  Resolution 15-19 Amending the FY 2014/15 Budget to Unappropriate Park Development
  Fees Related to Certain Capital Improvement Program Projects.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

12.  Annual Routine Maintenance Program for Sidewalk Grinding

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Mayor Schlicht asked for clarification on language in the staff report and bid
  specifications.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Rattay responded that the bids are
  based on an estimated number of problem areas.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to (1) award
  contract for the subject services to BPR, Inc. (A15-22) for the period of July 1, 2015
  through June 30, 2017 in the amount of $100,000.00; and (2) authorize issuance of a
  purchase order to BPR, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2015 through June 30, 2016, in an
  amount not to exceed $50,000.00 pending adoption of the 2015-2017 budget by City
  Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  6  May 18, 2015
 13.  Annual Maintenance Program for the Removal and Replacement of Concrete
  Sidewalks, Curb & Gutter, Driveway Approaches

  Mayor Schlicht asked if this contract is based on estimated areas of need as was explained
  for item 12.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Rattay responded affirmatively.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to (1) award
  contract for the subject services to S. Parker Engineering, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2015
  through June 30, 2017 in the amount of $657,000.00; and (2) authorize issuance of a
  purchase order to S. Parker Engineering for the period of July 1, 2015 through June 30,
  2016, in an amount not to exceed $328,500.00 pending adoption of the 2015-2017 budget
  by City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

14.  Annual Park and Facility Hardscape Construction Improvements

  Mayor Schlicht noted that the contract amount is lower than the bid amount.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Rattay responded that the contract is
  based on a representative sampling for estimated need.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to (1) award
  contract for the subject services to S. Parker Engineering, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2015
  through June 30, 2017 in the amount of $110,000.00; and (2) authorize issuance of a
  purchase order to S. Parker Engineering, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2015 through June
  30, 2016, in an amount not to exceed $55,000.00 pending adoption of the 2015-2017
  budget by City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

15.  Annual Maintenance Program for the Removal and Replacement of Asphalt
  Pavement and Related Services

City Council Minutes  7  May 18, 2015
   Council Member Sachs expressed concern that staff recommends awarding the contract to
  the second lowest bidder because the low bidder neglected to submit the addendum.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Schlicht, to rebid the project
  and add clarifying language to the RFP.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Sachs and Schlicht
  NOES:  Bucknum, Raths, and Ury
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  award contract for the subject services to Ben’s Asphalt, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2015,
  through June 30, 2017, in the amount of $540,000; (2) authorize issuance of a purchase
  order to Ben’s Asphalt, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2015, through June 30, 2016, in an
  amount not to exceed $270,000 pending adoption of the 2015-2017 budget by City
  Council; (3) award the secondary contract for the subject program to Sander’s Paving, Inc.,
  for the period of July 1, 2015, through June 30, 2017, in the amount of $360,000 and (4)
  authorize issuance of a purchase order to Sander’s Paving, Inc. for the period of July 1,
  2015, through June 30, 2016, in an amount not to exceed $180,000 pending approval of
  the 2015-2017 budget by City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, and Ury
  NOES:  Sachs and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

16.  Water Conservation - Turf Removal Program Grants Awarded

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Mayor Schlicht noted that the Community Services Commission will be addressing this
  matter tomorrow evening.

  Director Rattay clarified that there is misinformation being circulated and that staff is not
  recommending artificial turf in any city park.

  Mayor Schlicht expressed concern that the city is spending a lot of money on the drought
  and she recommended slowing down and making a plan.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 15-20 Amending Fiscal year 2014/15 Budget Recognizing Revenue from
  Water Conservation Grants Totaling $55,795.00; (2) approved Seventh Amendment to the
City Council Minutes  8  May 18, 2015
   existing purchasing agreement with John Deere Landscape, Inc. for the period of July 1,
  2013 through June 30, 2015 to increase the contract by an amount not to exceed $595,000;
  (3) amended existing purchase order to John Deere Landscape, Inc., #150011 by an amount
  not to exceed $25,000; (4) approved Second Amendment to the existing contract and issue
  a change order to A.C. Landscape Inc., for Technical Irrigation, by an amount not to
  exceed $30,000; and (5) approved Fifth Amendment to the existing contract and issue a
  change order to WM Vandergeest Landscape Care Inc. Area 6 not to exceed $50,000.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

22.  Designation of City Manager as Hearing Officer under City of Mission Viejo
  Discipline Personnel Policy

  Council Member Sachs asked for clarification on the current policy.

  City Attorney Curley outlined the policy and the recommendation to allow the City
  Manager to designate an independent hearing officer.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Ury, to confirm
  authorizing the City Manager to act as the City Council's Hearing Officer designee as
  allowed under the City of Mission Viejo Municipal Code and Discipline Personnel Policy
  by minute order.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

23.  Installation of Speed Humps on Via Burriana

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  At the hour of 7:30 p.m., Mayor Schlicht opened the public hearing.

  The following expressed support for the installation of speed humps on Via Burriana to
  help reduce the speed on the street: David Austin, M.V. and Kevin Weir, M.V.

City Council Minutes  9  May 18, 2015
   At the hour of 7:34 p.m., Mayor Schlicht closed the public hearing.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
  installation of speed humps on Via Burriana.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  Sachs
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour of 7:45 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 7:57
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

NEW BUSINESS

24.  Sale of Real Property: City Sale of Site C to Housing Authority

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report. Special Counsel Celeste Brady
  answered the City Council Members questions relative to the Housing Authority.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed his opposition to the sale of Site C to the Housing
  Authority.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  approve sale of property pursuant to attached Purchase and Sale Agreement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, release the
  appraisal on the property.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Raths and Schlicht
  NOES:  Bucknum, Sachs, and Ury
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  10  May 18, 2015
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the Orange County Fire Authority was attempting to
censure his public comments on agenda items at their Board Meetings however the majority of the
Board rejected the recommendation by a vote of 21-1. He also stated that OCFA is now attempting
to charge him for public records request programming costs.

25.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that he had nothing to report.

26.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that he attended the meeting on Council Member Sachs'
  behalf but he had nothing to report.

27.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury announced that he expects to have a full report on the OCTA budget
  at the next meeting.

STAFF REPORTS

28.  Legislative Update: AB1217 and SB355

  City Manager Wilberg provided the Council with an update on AB1217 and SB355.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

29.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum outlined her attendance at recent events including an Elks Club
scholarship dinner, the Angels of the Arts student showcase at Saddleback College, the Rotary
Prayer breakfast, a Southern California Association of Governments conference in Palm Springs,
and the National Day of Prayer event at the Potocki Center. She also discussed her attendance at
the city employee recognition luncheon and she noted that City Manager Wilberg and City Clerk
Hamman were both recognized for twenty-five years of service. Council Member Bucknum drew
the Council’s attention to upcoming events including the Chamber of Commerce monthly meeting
hosted by the Nadadores, the KSBR Birthday Bash, a dive meet at the Marguerite swim and dive
complex, and the city’s Memorial Day ceremony which begins at 8:30 a.m. at the civic center. In
City Council Minutes  11  May 18, 2015
 closing, Council Member Bucknum announced that she has been appointed to the Local Agency
Formation Commission and she is honored that she will be representing South County.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs announced that he has started a conversation with the City Manager about
the Orange County Sheriff's Department and he has requested a monthly report so that the Council
can start discussing, more formally, what that contract is providing for the City. Council Member
Sachs noted that he has begun to preview the draft budget and he asked that staff provide a cut to
the budget of .003% to establish an economic development fund. He also recommended that any
time expenditures are added to the budget, that they be offset with cuts to the budget. Council
Member Sachs asked for the status of the Planning and Transportation Commission's
recommendation to the Council on political signs and he announced that tomorrow he has a private
meeting with the CFO and Executive Chairman of the San Juan Hills Toll Road Agency to review
the proposed budget.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury announced that he had nothing to report.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

30.  Resolution Supporting Senate Constitutional Amendment 2 (SCA 2): Senator Nguyen

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths presented his report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to adopt
  Resolution 15-22 to support Senator Janet Nguyen's Senate Constitutional Amendment 2
  (SCA 2) to prohibit banning the U.S. flag on state funded college campuses in California.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  Sachs
  ABSENT:  None

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths congratulated and thanked Mission Viejo Ophthalmologist
  Dr. Ghosheh who recently installed 240 solar panels at his business.

Mayor Schlicht

31.  Require Non-Profit Organizations who receive public funding and/or resources from
  the City of Mission Viejo to submit its IRS Tax Form 990

City Council Minutes  12  May 18, 2015
   Mayor Schlicht presented her report.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to table the matter
  to a future date.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

Mayor Schlicht asked the City Attorney how she can go about creating a water committee.

City Attorney Curley responded that he will speak with her about the matter and she can place an
item on the agenda to see if the Council would like to move forward.

Mayor Schlicht announced that she and Mayor Pro Tem Raths met with Care Ambulance and she
asked some hard questions. Care is due to begin serving Mission Viejo on June 1 and she feels
confident that the City will continue to get good ambulance service. Mayor Schlicht encouraged
residents to attend tomorrow’s Community Services Commission meeting to participate in the
presentations and discussions on a proposed Youth Center and the review of the City’s drought
plan. She will be attending the meeting as a resident to express concern about a park near her
home in Aegean Hills. Mayor Schlicht closed the meeting in memory of her aunt, Mona Janise,
who always aimed for the best of everything and achieved it often. She was an inspiration to all
who knew her and she definitely made the world a better place to live. Mona Janise was an
incredible aunt, sister and mother. The Mayor then read a verse from 1 Corinthians 13:13: “And
now these three remain: faith, hope and love. But the greatest of these is love.”

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:12 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Schlicht adjourned the meeting in memory of her aunt, Mona Janise, to Monday, June 1,
2015, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of June 1, 2015

City Council Minutes  13  May 18, 2015
